Since Fame is a Unique Master how does contesting work with it?

Thanks,
~Matt Strehlow

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 9 Feb 2000, Matthew E Strehlow wrote:

> Since Fame is a Unique Master how does contesting work with it?

(Also see the errata on it).

The card is controlled by the Methuselah who played it, and each copy is
contested by whichever Methuselah played it - not the Methuselah whose
vampire it is on. When a copy is yielded, the other copy comes into play
during its controller's untap phase.

--

James Coupe

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Matthew E Strehlow wrote:
>
> Since Fame is a Unique Master how does contesting work with it?

Same as with any other card.

As with all master cards, Fame is controlled by the Methuselah
who played it.

The Methuselahs who control them pay one pool each untap or yield
their copy.
